prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures an outdoor nighttime walkway beside an arched building colonnade, showing a smooth bright-to-dark vertical gradient on the ground plane from roughly 1 to 10+ metres ahead, while no people or objects are within arm's reach (~1 m) of the camera wearer. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer first pans left toward the building facade and planted flowerbed (frames 1–3) and then pans back right along the open path (frames 4–5), with vertical pillars and tree trunks standing out at roughly 3–6 metres and a small cat visible in RGB frame 3 appearing as a faint protrusion near the left edge of the flowerbed at about 4 metres. In frame 3, the depth map clearly isolates two thin vertical trunks/poles (~5–6 m away, spaced ~2 m apart) and two short bollard lights (~3–4 m away) against the darker recessed facade (~7–9 m away), clarifying 3D layering that is blurred or lost in dark shadows in the RGB image. However, the map is unreliable around bright light sources and motion-blurred frames (especially frame 2), where it smooths over archway openings, merges background architecture into flat dark regions, and misses fine details like distant parked bicycles/motorcycles (~10–15 m away) and flush manhole covers.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is almost entirely blank (black) across all 5 frames, failing to detect the architectural columns, the walkway, the planted bed, the bollard lights, or the small cat (~4 m ahead on the left in frame 3), and confirms that no people or objects are within arm's reach. Its only outputs are two severe misclassifications: in frame 4, a large teal mask falsely labels the cobblestoned ground plane (spanning ~1 to 5 m in front of the wearer) as a 'bed', and in frame 5, a tiny cyan patch on the far right (~8–12 m away) labels a distant illuminated arch/pillar region as a 'car'. While the top contour of the 'bed' mask in frame 4 roughly follows the boundary where the flat pavement meets the raised planter and building pillars (~4–5 m away) as the camera turns right, it provides no advantage over the RGB strip. Overall, the segmentation map is completely unreliable in this low-light, motion-blurred outdoor scene, missing true objects while hallucinating indoor and vehicular classes.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, containing no yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. Cross-referencing with the RGB strip confirms that this absence of detections is spatially accurate: there are no other people present to face, look toward, approach, or retreat from the camera wearer as the viewpoint pans left and then right along the walkway. Furthermore, the camera wearer's own hands and arms remain entirely out of the field of view below or behind the camera throughout the sequence, so nothing is shown interacting within arm's reach. While the pose map is reliable in avoiding false-positive human skeletons on tree trunks, pillars, or the small cat in frame 3, it offers no spatial information beyond confirming an empty, person-free environment.
